decision: Approve all three exact challenger replacements after complete endpoint and original-statement review. Retain the CY/topological-computation method direction as withheld and separately admit the explicitly stated connection as related_question. Retain Hartle–Hawking related_question rather than whole containment and the corrected charge-expansion qualification. Other joint withholdings remain optional pending.

proposal.title: Use enumerative and quantum-geometric computations in geometry questions
proposal.rationale: The paired statements identify enumerative and quantum-geometric computations as the method connection. Those computations are organized in s10 and can serve compatible invariant-computation questions in s27.
proposal.qualification: This route concerns the stated computational connection, not every construction or classification target. Fourfold quantum cohomology is not identified with every topological-string amplitude problem. Preserve local versus compact geometry, genus and dimension, including the distinction between four-dimensional reflexive polytopes and Calabi–Yau fourfolds. The noncompact toric vertex and large-Calabi–Yau isolated spherical M2 setting retain their domains; no exhaustive classification or identification of physical phases follows.

approvedExactReplacement.title: Pending: orient the enumerative and quantum-geometric method connection
approvedExactReplacement.rationale: Both original statements identify a methodological connection, but neither identifies which endpoint supplies the computation and which target it serves. Both endpoints contain computational questions. The proposal's reversal assumes that computations organized in s10 serve s27's construction or invariant targets; that applicability is not established merely by their computational character.
approvedExactReplacement.qualification: Keep the stated enumerative and quantum-geometric connection visible. Fourfold quantum cohomology is not identified with every topological-string amplitude target. Any resolved method route must preserve local versus compact geometry, genus and dimension, including the distinction between four-dimensional reflexive polytopes and Calabi–Yau fourfolds. The noncompact toric vertex and large-Calabi–Yau isolated spherical M2 settings retain their domains. No exhaustive classification, common Kähler cone or identification of physical phases follows.
approvedExactReplacement.missingPremise: Identify the supplied computation, its provider endpoint, and the recipient target for which it is applicable: a computation from s27 serving a protected-amplitude or BPS question in s10, or a computation from s10 serving a construction or invariant question in s27. The paired statements and the fourfold quantum-cohomology caveat do not resolve that mapping.

proposal.title: Specialize inflationary selection to Hartle–Hawking histories
proposal.rationale: The Hartle–Hawking state and specified additional criteria in s12 refine s7's questions about quantum initial configurations, weighting and the allowability of inflation. The broader question supplies a scope, rather than an underlying method being applied.
proposal.qualification: Relative weighting under distance or refined-de-Sitter criteria remains distinct from excluding complex saddles through KS allowability. The KS branch retains four-dimensional O(4)-symmetric minisuperspace and does not establish sufficiency for arbitrary interacting quantum field theories. Potential selection and tensor predictions remain tied to the state, criterion and investigated models; the reported approximate r below 0.08 concerns their 50–60 e-fold histories. Selection does not by itself demonstrate a dynamical exit.

approvedExactReplacement.title: Examine Hartle–Hawking weighting and complex-saddle allowability
approvedExactReplacement.rationale: The shared no-boundary and inflationary-selection setting supports the stated connection. However, s12 also targets complex-saddle allowability and observable predictions, including potential selection and tensors; the packet does not establish full containment of these targets within s7's initial-condition, weighting and transition scope. The original application language also does not identify a particular underlying method supplied by s7.
approvedExactReplacement.qualification: Retain Einstein gravity with a scalar and the Hartle–Hawking state. Relative weighting under distance or refined-de-Sitter criteria differs from excluding complex saddles through KS allowability. The KS branch retains four-dimensional O(4)-symmetric minisuperspace and does not establish sufficiency for arbitrary interacting quantum field theories. Potential selection and tensor predictions remain tied to the state, criterion and investigated models. The reported approximate r below 0.08 concerns their 50–60 e-fold histories in the supplied 9 November 2023 v2 context. Weighting remains conditional on its adopted prescription and does not demonstrate a dynamical exit.

proposal.title: Use controlled charge expansions to investigate charged-dimension inequalities
proposal.rationale: Controlled charge expansions and applicable Goldstone descriptions provide methods for studying charged dimensions and testing scoped inequality questions. They do not themselves establish a universal inequality.
proposal.qualification: Apply only the overlapping systems and controlled regimes, preserving source-specific large-charge, leading-N and dimensional assumptions. Large f can occur outside the large-charge regime. Goldstone-family convexity requires lowest scalar states sharing the stated Goldstone realization and does not extend across competing families. Fixed-spin minima need not equal unrestricted charge-sector minima; effective-potential convexity and continuous convexity do not establish discrete charge superadditivity. Minimum charge, chosen spacing and onset remain distinct. Defect and nonrelativistic applications do not automatically transfer, and an EFT without a known UV completion does not establish a CFT counterexample.
